sections.overview: The smooth stingray is a very large Indo-Pacific ray now classified as Bathytoshia brevicaudata; older sources use Dasyatis.
sections.identification: It has rows of small white spots beside the head and a relatively short tail; the similar black stingray B. lata lacks those spots.
sections.habitat: It lives on the bottom in coastal waters and estuaries, from shallow water to about 170 m.
sections.diet: It feeds on bottom-dwelling fishes, crustaceans and bivalves, often dug from sediment.
sections.behavior: It is often inquisitive around divers, but its venomous tail spine can cause severe injury.
sections.reproduction: It is aplacental viviparous and females produce litters of about six to ten pups.
sections.ecology: A bottom-feeding predator, it is also caught as bycatch in several coastal fisheries.
sections.conservation: The 2020 global IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern, with a stable trend.
